t:
(a) 
Section 301 of the National Security Act of 1947 is amended to read as follows:


“Sec. 301.

(a) 
The Secretary of Defense shall receive the compensation prescribed by law for heads of executive departments.


“(b) 
The Deputy Secretary of Defense shall receive compensation at the rate of $14,500 a year, or such other compensation plus $500 a year as may hereafter be provided by law for under secretaries of executive departments. The Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of the Air Force shall each receive compensation at the rate of $14,000 a year, or such other compensation as may hereafter be provided by law for under secretaries of executive departments.”




 
    (b) 
Section 302 of the National Security Act of 1947 is amended to read as follows:

“Sec. 302.
The Assistant Secretaries of Defense and the Under Secretaries and Assistant Secretaries of the Army, the Navy, and the Air Force shall each receive compensation at the rate of $10,330 a year or at the rate hereafter prescribed by law for assistant secretaries of executive departments and shall perform such duties as the respective Secretaries may prescribe.”



 
    (c) 
Section 303 (a) of the National Security Act of 1947 is amended to read as follows:

“(a) 
The Secretary of Defense, the Chairman of the National Security Resources Board, the Director of Central Intelligence, and the National Security Council, acting through its Executive Secretary, are authorized to appoint such advisory committees and to employ, consistent with other provisions of this Act, such part-time advisory personnel as they may deem necessary in carrying out their respective functions and the functions of agencies under their control. Persons holding other offices or positions under the United States for which they receive compensation, while serving as members of such committees, shall receive no additional compensation for such service. Other members of such committees and other part-time advisory personnel so employed may serve without compensation or may receive compensation at a rate not to exceed $50 for each day of service, as determined by the appointing authority.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this section only sets salaries for federal officials, which would be purely internal to the government. But subsection (c) authorizes the Secretary of Defense and other officials to appoint advisory committees, and it separates members who already hold federal office from "other members" who may serve unpaid or for up to $50 per day. That distinction implies the committees include people from outside the federal government advising on federal functions, which counts as participation even though the authority is discretionary.
fable.s: are authorized to appoint such advisory committees and to employ, consistent with other provisions of this Act, such part-time advisory personnel as they may deem necessary in carrying out their respective functions

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly authorizes federal officials to appoint 'advisory committees' and 'part-time advisory personnel.' The definition states that participation includes advisory committees, boards, or panels that include non-federal members. The text further distinguishes these members from federal employees by stating that persons holding other federal offices receive no additional compensation, while 'other members' may receive compensation, implying the existence of outside, non-federal participants. This fits the definition of participation involving outsiders in the decision-making or advisory process.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Defense, the Chairman of the National Security Resources Board, the Director of Central Intelligence, and the National Security Council, acting through its Executive Secretary, are authorized to appoint such advisory committees and to employ, consistent with other provisions of this Act, such part-time advisory personnel as they may deem necessary in carrying out their respective functions and the functions of agencies under their control.

opus.w: The amended Section 303(a) lets the Secretary of Defense and other national security officials appoint advisory committees to advise on their functions. The text separates federal officeholders from 'other members' who may be unpaid or receive a per-diem rate, so people outside the government can serve on these committees. The rest of the section only sets pay for federal officials, which on its own would be 'No', but the advisory-committee provision brings outside parties into federal decision-making.
opus.s: are authorized to appoint such advisory committees and to employ, consistent with other provisions of this Act, such part-time advisory personnel as they may deem necessary in carrying out their respective functions and the functions of agencies under their control. Persons holding other offices or positions under the United States for which they receive compensation, while serving as members of such committees, shall receive no additional compensation for such service. Other members of such committees and other part-time advisory personnel so employed may serve without compensation or may receive compensation at a rate not to exceed $50 for each day of service
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** Most of this section only sets pay for federal officials, such as the Secretary of Defense and the Assistant Secretaries. That is purely internal to the federal government and would point to "No."

**Why that reading fails:** The amended Section 303(a) lets federal officials appoint advisory committees and part-time advisers to help them carry out their functions. The text separates committee members who already hold federal positions from "other members," who may serve unpaid or receive a per-diem rate. That means people from outside the government can sit on these advisory committees. Under the definition, an advisory committee with non-federal members counts as participation (compare Example 8).

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes federal officials to appoint advisory committees but does not require that these committees include non-federal members. It explicitly allows federal employees to serve on these committees, suggesting they may be composed entirely of insiders. Since the definition requires involvement of parties outside the federal government, and this text only describes internal staffing authority, it is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Defense, the Chairman of the National Security Resources Board, the Director of Central Intelligence, and the National Security Council, acting through its Executive Secretary, are authorized to appoint such advisory committees and to employ, consistent with other provisions of this Act, such part-time advisory personnel as they may deem necessary in carrying out their respective functions and the functions of agencies under their control. Persons holding other offices or positions under the United States for which they receive compensation, while serving as members of such committees, shall receive no additional compensation for such service.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "advisory committees" and "advisory personnel."
Resolution: The text allows federal officials (Secretary of Defense, Chairman of NSRB, Director of Central Intelligence, National Security Council) to appoint advisory committees. However, it does not specify that these committees must include non-federal members. In fact, it explicitly states that persons holding other federal offices can serve without additional compensation, implying the committees may consist entirely of federal employees. Without a requirement or clear indication that non-federal outsiders are involved, this is intra-governmental coordination or staffing, not public participation.
